Order 
The present Writ Petition has been filed for the issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to quash the impugned order passed by the 3rd respondent in Na.Ka.No.1099/A1/UPaaThaSa/2025 dated 05.06.2025 and consequently direct the respondents to deseal the petitioner's Aathiyappan Petty Shop.
2. The petitioner runs a small petty shop selling fruits and other food items.
The respondents have alleged that the petitioner is selling banned items, namely tobacco.
This is the third time the respondents have imposed fine.
In the previous two instances, the petitioner paid the appropriate fine, and the shop was allowed to reopen.
3. In the present case, now the petitioner contended that the respondents without seizing any material has sealed the shop.
Moreover, no notice was issued.
4. On instructions, the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for respondents 1 and 2 submitted that 195 grams of tobacco were https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on:
26/06/2025 08:24:43 pm ) seized.
The respondents have not clarified whether the tobacco was kept for personal consumption or for commercial purposes.
Since the quantity is considered a consumable amount, this Court is inclined to quash the impugned order.
5. Accordingly, this writ petition is allowed.
The impugned order passed by the 3rd respondent in Na.Ka.No.1099/A1/UPaaThaSa/2025, dated 05.06.2025, is hereby quashed.
However, the petitioner is directed to submit an undertaking affidavit stating that he will not keep the said products in his shop in the future to the respondents.

The petitioner is further directed to pay a sum of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) in favor of the Government Orphanage, Madurai,
Savings Bank Account No.37487255860, IFSC: SBIN0007922, within a period of one week from today, i.e., by 25.06.2025.
Upon such payment and submission of the undertaking affidavit, the respondents are directed to reopen the shop within a period of three weeks thereafter.
Consequently, connected miscella- neous petitions are closed.
